summary: Double-precision float classification routine operating on the x87 stack (a1@st1, a2@st0). Stores the two doubles into locals, then inspects a2's exponent bits in its high word. If the exponent field (mask 0x7FFF0000) is non-zero the function immediately calls FloatingPointRemainder with mode 0. Otherwise it ORs a2's low words into a candidate result; when a2 is non-zero it scales the inputs by the read-only constant dbl_5E7514 (with a1 additionally scaled when a1's exponent field is <= 0x7FBE, selecting mode 3 instead of mode 2) and calls FloatingPointRemainder with the chosen mode. A zero a2 returns the low-word combination directly.

operations.description: Copy the two stack doubles into locals: a1 into v6 and a2 into v4.
Classify a2: test (high-word DWORD at v4+6) & 0x7FFF0000; non-zero exponent field selects the special-value path.
Call FloatingPointRemainder with mode 0 on the special-value path.
Combine a2's low words (v4[4] | v4[0]) into the candidate result used when a2 is zero.
Branch on a2 != 0.0; a zero a2 returns the combined low-word result directly.
Select default mode 2 and scale a2 by the read-only double constant dbl_5E7514.
When a1's exponent field ((WORD4(v6)) & 0x7FFFu) is <= 0x7FBE, promote the mode to 3 and scale a1 by dbl_5E7514.
Call FloatingPointRemainder with the selected mode (2 or 3) and the scaled operands.
Return the combined low-word result when a2 is zero (no remainder call).

unresolved: Exact semantics of FloatingPointRemainder's extra packed arguments (the __int128/word slices) are not recoverable from this function alone.
Value of dbl_5E7514 is not in the packet; it acts as a scaling constant for the classification path.
Bit field layout (high/low words) of the two doubles is implied by the pointer casts but not independently verified.
